nom: The Stuarts, the Civil War & the Glorious Revolution
cartes: Charles I succeeds his father James I
Gunpowder Plot: Guy Fawkes is arrested
4 November 1605
Guy Fawkes is executed for treason
January 1606
Petition of Right; Charles I dissolves Parliament for 11 years
Puritans sail on the Mayflower to America
Scottish Presbyterians rebel and twice beat the king's army
Catholic uprising in Ireland
Start of the English Civil War (Parliament against the king)
August 1642
English Civil War
Charles I is found guilty of treason and executed
30 January 1649
Commonwealth: monarchy abolished, Cromwell rules
Protectorate (Cromwell as Lord Protector)
Parliament bans Christmas celebrations
Cromwell massacres the people of Drogheda and Wexford in Ireland
Cromwell's Act of Settlement: land of Irish Catholics is confiscated
Catholics own 59% of the land in Ireland (less than 20% after 1652)
Death of Oliver Cromwell; his son Richard becomes Lord Protector
MPs invite Charles II to return as king
Reign of Charles II
Restoration of the monarchy period
Charles II's secret treaty with Louis XIV of France (to reconvert England to Catholicism)
Great Fire of London; anti-Catholic riots (22 dead)
Test Acts (exclude non-Anglicans from public office, universities, legal careers)
Two-year conflict between Charles II and Parliament over the succession of the Catholic James
James II becomes king (pro-Catholic policy)
Birth of James II's son, baptised a Catholic
Parliament secretly invites William of Orange; James II flees to France
November 1688
James II's armies are beaten in Ireland
Glorious Revolution (James II replaced by William and Mary)
Act of Settlement: a Catholic can no longer take the throne
Abolition of the Act of Settlement
Bill of Rights (limits the monarch's powers)
